nchemistry-9-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about hydrogen as a fuel?
o: It produces only water when used
It releases carbon monoxide when burnt
It emits no sulphur dioxide or particulates
nchemistry-9-3.x: Hydrogen gives only water, with zero carbon, CO, SO2 and particulate emissions, so the claim that it releases CO is false.

nchemistry-9-9.s: Which gas do CNG and LPG still release on burning, although they are cleaner than petrol and diesel?
nchemistry-9-9.x: CNG and LPG give far less CO, unburnt hydrocarbons and soot, but they still release CO2.

nenvironment-11-3.s: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight drives reactions between hydrocarbons and:
nenvironment-11-3.x: Sunlight makes nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicles react into ozone and PAN, forming photochemical smog.

n56f15c74e81.s: Under the National Clean Air Programme, the CPCB coordinates implementation with:
n56f15c74e81.x: NCAP is coordinated by the CPCB with the State Pollution Control Boards, not by the CPCB alone.

n3be64c3ced3.s: On India's Air Quality Index, a value of 301-400 falls in which category?
n3be64c3ced3.x: AQI 301-400 is Very poor; 201-300 is Poor and 401-500 is Severe.

nd310a618bad.s: How many pollutants are covered under India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards?
nd310a618bad.x: NAAQS cover 12 pollutants, including PM10, PM2.5, SO2, NO2, CO, O3, NH3, lead, benzene, benzo(a)pyrene, arsenic and nickel.

n7b99a66ee35.s: The National Air Quality Index covers how many pollutants?
n7b99a66ee35.x: The NAQI covers eight pollutants - PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb - on a 0-500 scale.

nfcd3e4c50b9.s: In 2024-25, how many of the 130 NCAP cities met the NAAQS for PM10?
nfcd3e4c50b9.x: Only 22 of the 130 NCAP cities met the PM10 standard, though 103 recorded a reduction compared with 2017-18.

nda796d762a7.s: BS-III emission norms began on 1 April 2005 in the NCR and how many other cities?
nda796d762a7.x: BS-III started from 1 April 2005 in the NCR and 10 other cities; BS-VI came nationwide on 1 April 2020.

n4fda6bc3f81.s: The APPCB state-level air-quality action plan covers how many urban local bodies?
n4fda6bc3f81.x: The plan covers 123 urban local bodies, including 17 municipal corporations.

nc4fcf796c03.s: Which industrial device removes coarse particles by centrifugal force?
nc4fcf796c03.x: Cyclone separators remove coarse particles by centrifugal force; wet scrubbers remove gases and particles, bag filters use fabric.

n98833a3c6e4.s: Which vehicular pollutant is a carcinogen linked to leukaemia?
n98833a3c6e4.x: Benzene is a carcinogen linked to leukaemia; NOx forms ground-level ozone and acid rain, and CO forms carboxyhaemoglobin.

nd5d006ba949.s: BS-VII, planned for 2026-27, is expected to be equivalent to:
nd5d006ba949.x: BS-VII, the planned next step after BS-VI (Euro 6), is expected to be equivalent to Euro 7.

nenvironment-36-20.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about photochemical smog?
o: Nitrogen oxides are one of its inputs
Hydrocarbons are one of its inputs
It can form in the absence of sunlight
nenvironment-36-20.x: Photochemical smog forms when NOx and hydrocarbons react under sunlight, so it cannot form without sunlight.

n5f9d7870deb.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: COD – Oxygen needed to oxidise all organic matter, biodegradable and non-biodegradable
BOD – Oxygen needed to oxidise all organic matter, biodegradable and non-biodegradable
High BOD – Clean water with little organic matter
COD – Oxygen bacteria need to decompose organic matter
n5f9d7870deb.x: COD is the oxygen needed to oxidise all organic matter; BOD is the oxygen bacteria need to decompose it, and high BOD means heavy organic pollution.

nbc4ccec3e08.s: The coliform count of a water sample indicates:
nbc4ccec3e08.x: Coliform count indicates faecal contamination; NTU measures turbidity and TDS represents dissolved salts.

nf37e2ab6018.s: Under CPCB criteria, the total coliform limit for Class A water is:
nf37e2ab6018.x: Class A (drinking source after disinfection, without conventional treatment) allows total coliform up to 50 MPN/100 ml.

naa5048b168c.s: AMRUT 2.0 mandates what share of reuse of treated urban wastewater?
naa5048b168c.x: AMRUT 2.0 mandates 20 per cent reuse of treated wastewater, not 50 per cent.

na1139d5e8e5.s: Which is the most nutrient-enriched trophic state of a water body?
na1139d5e8e5.x: Water bodies progress from oligotrophic to mesotrophic to eutrophic and, at extreme enrichment, hypereutrophic.

ne4455f7b2e6.s: The first dolphin estimate under the Namami Gange Mission (March 2025) counted how many dolphins?
ne4455f7b2e6.x: The first dolphin estimate (March 2025) counted 6,327 dolphins.

new.s: Per the CAQM synthesis report (January 2026), the largest primary contributor to NCR's winter air pollution is:
new.x: Transport is the largest primary contributor in the NCR, about 23% of the winter load.

new.s: Which of the following fuels is the most polluting?
new.x: Coal gives high CO2, SO2, NOx, PM and ash, making it the most polluting; LPG, CNG and biogas emit far less.

new.s: Between petrol and diesel, diesel is known to emit more:
new.x: Both emit CO2, CO, NOx, unburnt hydrocarbons and PM, but diesel gives more particulate matter than petrol.

new.s: Classical (London) smog forms under which conditions?
o: Warm, sunny weather with NOx and VOCs
Cold, humid weather with SO2, smoke and fog
new.x: London smog forms from SO2, smoke and particulates with fog in cold, humid weather; Los Angeles smog needs warm sunshine.

new.s: The Asian Brown Cloud over South Asia appears mainly during:
new.x: The Asian Brown Cloud of soot, black carbon and sulphate aerosols forms in the dry season, January–March.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a secondary pollutant?
new.x: Lead from vehicles is a primary pollutant; ozone, PAN and ammonium sulphate form in the air.

new.s: Magnetite particles from combustion and brake wear, found in brain tissue, are possibly linked to:
new.x: Magnetite particles have been found in brain tissue and are possibly linked to Alzheimer's disease.

new.s: Which air pollutant is chiefly associated with brain damage, high blood pressure and kidney damage?
new.x: Lead from leaded petrol and smelters causes brain damage, high blood pressure and kidney damage.

new.s: Carbon monoxide's affinity for haemoglobin is about how many times that of oxygen?
new.x: CO binds haemoglobin 200–250 times more readily than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and causing hypoxia.

new.s: Fertilisers and livestock together account for about what share of ammonia emissions?
new.x: Fertilisers and livestock contribute 77–80% of ammonia, which drives secondary particle formation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about ozone:
1. Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant.
2. Stratospheric ozone shields the Earth from UV radiation.
3. Ground-level ozone is emitted directly by vehicles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ground-level ozone forms in the air (secondary) and is not emitted directly, so 3 is wrong; stratospheric ozone is the UV shield.

new.s: Which group suffers most from indoor air pollution?
new.x: Indoor smoke from solid fuels hits women and children the most, causing COPD, lung cancer and heart disease.

new.s: Which radioactive gas is a recognised indoor air pollutant?
new.x: Radon is listed among indoor pollutants along with smoke, mould, CO and mosquito coils.

new.s: Mosses are used as bioindicators of:
new.x: Mosses indicate heavy-metal deposition, while lichens indicate SO2.

new.s: India's NAAQS annual limit for PM2.5 is:
new.x: India's annual PM2.5 limit is 40 µg/m³, eight times laxer than the WHO 2021 guideline of 5 µg/m³.

new.s: Fossil-fuel air pollution caused about how many premature deaths in India in 2022?
new.x: About 1.72 million premature deaths in India (2022) were linked to fossil-fuel air pollution; 7 million is WHO's global figure.

new.s: India's NAAQS 24-hour limit for SO2 is:
new.x: The 24-hour SO2 limit is 80 µg/m³; the annual limits are 50 (urban) and 20 (ecologically sensitive).

new.s: In the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2025, India was ranked the world's ____ most polluted country.
new.x: India was 6th in 2025 (5th in 2024); Pakistan was the most polluted country.

new.s: According to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2025, the world's most polluted city was:
new.x: Loni (UP) was the most polluted city in 2025; Bhiwadi topped in 2021 and Delhi was 4th.

new.s: Per the IQAir 2025 report, what share of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline?
new.x: Only 14% of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline in the 2025 report.

new.s: India's National Air Quality Index was developed at:
new.x: The NAQI, launched on 6 April 2015 under Swachh Bharat, was developed at IIT Kanpur and is run by the CPCB.

new.s: Which AQI category is correctly matched with its colour?
new.x: Severe is maroon; Poor is orange, Very Poor red and Satisfactory light green.

new.s: SAMEER, the app that gives air-quality data from CAAQMS, belongs to:
new.x: SAMEER is the CPCB's app; SAFAR-AIR is the MoES app.

new.s: Which pollutants does NAMP regularly monitor at all locations?
new.x: NAMP, started by the CPCB in 1984, regularly monitors SO2, NO2, PM10 and PM2.5 at all locations.

new.s: The original NCAP target of a 20–30% PM cut by 2024 used which base year?
new.x: The original target was a 20–30% PM cut by 2024 over 2017; the revised one uses 2017-18.

new.s: NCAP covers 130 cities in how many States/UTs?
new.x: NCAP covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs, including non-attainment and Million Plus cities.

new.s: The legal basis of the National Clean Air Programme is the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
new.x: NCAP rests on the Air Act, 1981.

new.s: According to the NGT (May 2026), about what share of NCAP spending went to road dust?
new.x: The NGT found 86% of NCAP spending went to road dust.

new.s: The PRANA portal for NCAP was launched in:
new.x: PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities) was launched on 7 September 2021.

new.s: The Methanol Economy programme is associated with:
new.x: The Methanol Economy is a NITI Aayog initiative among cleaner-fuel measures.

new.s: The SATAT initiative promotes:
new.x: SATAT is the compressed biogas programme; green hydrogen has its own National Mission.

new.s: Which scheme gives subsidies for electric vehicles as a vehicular-emission control measure?
new.x: FAME-II gives EV subsidies; SATAT is for compressed biogas and PRANA is the NCAP portal.

new.s: India's vehicle scrappage policy was introduced in:
new.x: The vehicle scrappage policy came in 2021, alongside PUC and RFID pollution charges.

new.s: OCEMS is mandatory in Delhi-NCR for which category of industries?
new.x: Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems are mandatory for red-category industries in Delhi-NCR.

new.s: Under GRAP, Stage III is invoked when the AQI is in the range:
new.x: GRAP Stage III corresponds to Severe (401–450); Stage IV is Severe+ above 450.

new.s: Which GRAP stage is correctly matched with its AQI category?
new.x: Stage IV is Severe+ above 450; Stage I is Poor, Stage II Very Poor and Stage III Severe (401–450).

new.s: The Centrally Sponsored Scheme on crop residue management machinery began in:
new.x: The CSS on crop residue machinery dates from 2018, supporting in-situ management such as the Happy Seeder.

new.s: The Happy Seeder is used for:
new.x: The Happy Seeder is subsidised machinery for in-situ management of stubble.

new.s: CAQM banned the use of coal in Delhi-NCR from:
new.x: Coal was banned in Delhi-NCR from 1 January 2023 by the statutory CAQM.

new.s: Normal rain has a pH of about 5.6 because of dissolved:
new.x: Normal rain is about pH 5.6 due to carbonic acid; acid rain is below 5.6.

new.s: Nitric acid accounts for about ____ of the acidity of acid rain.
new.x: H2SO4 gives about two-thirds of the acidity and HNO3 about one-third.

new.s: A fall of one unit in pH means the acidity increases:
new.x: pH is logarithmic: each step is a tenfold change in acidity.

new.s: The Taj Trapezium Zone covers an area of about:
new.x: The TTZ, about 10,400 sq km, protects the Taj, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.

new.s: In which year did the Supreme Court, in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India, bar coal and coke in the Taj Trapezium Zone?
new.x: In 1996 the SC barred coal/coke in the TTZ, requiring a shift to natural gas or relocation.

new.s: Which country was the world's largest emitter of SO2 in 2022?
new.x: India was the largest SO2 emitter in 2022, with over 20% of the total.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a preventive measure against acid rain?
new.x: Liming is remedial, treating already acidified lakes; the others cut emissions.

new.s: The first binding international treaty on transboundary air pollution was the:
new.x: The UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (Geneva, 1979) was the first binding treaty.

new.s: Which protocol under LRTAP is correctly matched with its focus?
new.x: Sofia (1988) froze NOx; Helsinki (1985) sought a 30% sulphur cut; Gothenburg (1999) covers SO2, NOx, NH3 and VOCs.

new.s: How many NCAP non-attainment cities are in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has 13 non-attainment cities, including Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Guntur, Nellore and Kurnool.

new.s: The Krishnapatnam thermal power plant is in which area of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Krishnapatnam is at Nellore; Dr NTTPS is at Vijayawada and Simhadri at Visakhapatnam.

new.s: School Eco-Clubs in Andhra Pradesh that spread air-quality awareness run under:
new.x: AP school Eco-Clubs run under the AP National Green Corps (2002-03).

new.s: In Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026, which Vijayawada ward ranked 2nd nationally?
new.x: Vijayawada ward 60 ranked 2nd nationally; ward 31 was the best in the State.

new.s: Euro-based emission norms began in India under the Bharat Stage name in:
new.x: The Bharat Stage name began in 2000 with BS-I; 1991 saw only the first petrol norms.

new.s: BS-I emission norms were also known as:
new.x: BS-I, introduced nationwide on 1 April 2000, was also called India 2000.

new.s: BS-III emission norms were implemented nationwide in:
new.x: BS-III came to the NCR and 10 cities in 2005 and nationwide in 2010.

new.s: BS-II emission norms were implemented nationwide in:
new.x: BS-II began in Delhi on 1 April 2000 and went nationwide in 2005.

new.s: In 2010, BS-IV norms were first introduced in how many cities?
new.x: BS-IV started in 13 cities in 2010 and went nationwide in April 2017.

new.s: The Supreme Court barred the sale and registration of BS-IV vehicles from:
new.x: In 2018 the SC ordered no sale or registration of BS-IV vehicles from 1 April 2020.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India skipping BS-V:
1. The decision was taken in 2016.
2. Urgent air pollution in Delhi-NCR was one reason.
3. BS-V was enforced in 13 cities before being dropped.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 2016 decision moved BS-IV straight to BS-VI because of Delhi-NCR pollution; BS-V was never implemented anywhere.

new.s: The fuel-sulphur limit under BS-IV was:
new.x: BS-IV allowed 50 ppm sulphur; BS-VI cut it to 10 ppm.

new.s: Under BS-VI, the NOx limit for diesel cars is:
new.x: BS-VI limits NOx to 80 mg/km for diesel and 60 mg/km for petrol; 4.5 mg/km is the diesel PM limit.

new.s: The fuel-sulphur limit under BS-III was:
new.x: Fuel sulphur was 500 ppm under BS-II, 350 under BS-III, 50 under BS-IV and 10 under BS-VI.

new.s: Lead from vehicle exhaust acts chiefly as a:
new.x: Lead is a neurotoxin; leaded petrol was phased out by 2000. Benzene is the leukaemia carcinogen.

new.s: SCR systems in BS-VI diesel vehicles convert NOx into nitrogen and water using:
new.x: Selective Catalytic Reduction uses urea-based AdBlue to turn NOx into N2 and water.

new.s: Which BS-VI system monitors emissions and alerts the driver?
new.x: On-Board Diagnostics (OBD-II) monitors emissions and alerts the driver; DPF traps soot.

new.s: Multi-point fuel injection, introduced in the BS-II era, replaced:
new.x: Multi-point fuel injection replaced carburettors in the BS-II era.

new.s: Under the E20 rollout from 1 April 2026, petrol must have a minimum octane rating (RON) of:
new.x: E20 requires a minimum RON of 95, not 91.

new.s: Under the CAFE III third draft, the norms apply to cars from:
new.x: The CAFE III draft (16 July 2026) applies to cars from April 2027, with targets relaxed by about 21%.

new.s: The Vehicle Scrappage Policy (2021) relies on Automated Testing Stations and:
new.x: The policy works through Automated Testing Stations and Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities.

new.s: Officers for PUC testing are trained at ARAI Pune and:
new.x: PUC officers are trained at ARAI Pune and IIP Dehradun.

new.s: Fuel sulphur in India was cut from 500 ppm to 10 ppm over about:
new.x: Refinery upgrades cut sulphur from 500 to 10 ppm in about 15 years.

new.s: Which of the following is a point pollutant discharge into water?
new.x: Point pollution comes from sewage outfalls and effluent pipes; agricultural and urban runoff are non-point.

new.s: Sand mining in rivers mainly raises water:
new.x: Sand mining raises turbidity and degrades river beds.

new.s: Besides ritual offerings, which effluent can have a BOD far above sewage and deplete DO fast?
new.x: Dairy effluent and ritual offerings can have BOD far higher than sewage, depleting DO quickly.

new.s: Clean water has a BOD below:
new.x: Clean water has BOD below 4.0 mg/L; DO above 8.0 mg/L is the clean value for dissolved oxygen.

new.s: Which of the following is a dissolved solid in water?
new.x: Sodium salts and nitrate pass the filter (dissolved); silt and clay are suspended solids.

new.s: Under BIS IS 10500, the limit for nitrate in drinking water is:
new.x: BIS sets nitrate at 45 mg/L, while WHO uses 50 mg/L.

new.s: The WHO guideline value for nitrate in drinking water is:
new.x: WHO sets 50 mg/L for nitrate; BIS sets 45 mg/L.

new.s: Under BIS IS 10500, the limit for uranium in drinking water is:
new.x: BIS sets uranium at 30 ppb.

new.s: For CPCB Class B (outdoor bathing) water, the BOD must not exceed:
new.x: Class B allows BOD up to 3 mg/L with DO of at least 5 mg/L; Class A allows BOD up to 2.

new.s: CPCB Class C water (drinking after conventional treatment) allows total coliform up to:
new.x: Class C allows 5,000; Class B 500; Class A 50 MPN/100 ml.

new.s: In eutrophication, the decay of algal blooms causes:
new.x: Decomposing algae use up dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxia and fish kills.

new.s: Blackfoot disease is caused by:
new.x: Arsenicosis and blackfoot disease are caused by arsenic; cadmium causes itai-itai and mercury Minamata.

new.s: Minamata disease was first reported from Japan in:
new.x: Minamata disease (methyl mercury) was reported in Japan in 1956; itai-itai was first reported in 1912.

new.s: Dental fluorosis mainly affects children under the age of:
new.x: Dental fluorosis affects children under 8.

new.s: High uranium in groundwater is reported from which region of Punjab?
new.x: Uranium contamination is associated with the Malwa region of Punjab.

new.s: About what share of India's districts exceed 45 mg/L nitrate in groundwater?
new.x: Nitrate exceeds 45 mg/L in 56% of districts, mainly from fertilisers.

new.s: Roughly what share of India's urban sewage is treated (2026)?
new.x: Only about 28% of urban sewage is treated; 72% is discharged untreated.

new.s: The first sewage treatment plant under the Hybrid Annuity Model was at:
new.x: The first HAM STP came up at Haridwar in December 2019.

new.s: The Hybrid Annuity Model was approved for Namami Gange in:
new.x: HAM was approved in January 2016 with 100% central funding, its first use in sewage.

new.s: The Tiruppur textile cluster in Tamil Nadu is an example of:
new.x: Tiruppur is the cited example of Zero Liquid Discharge.

new.s: How many CETPs does Andhra Pradesh run?
new.x: AP runs 9 CETPs and has directed Zero Liquid Discharge.

new.s: Ganga Action Plan-I was launched in 1985 at:
new.x: Rajiv Gandhi launched GAP-I at Varanasi in 1985, covering 25 main-stem towns.

new.s: The National River Conservation Plan covers how many rivers in 16 States?
new.x: NRCP covers 38 rivers in 16 States, including the Godavari and Krishna.

new.s: Which of the following lakes is NOT covered under the National Lake Conservation Plan?
new.x: NLCP covers urban lakes such as Bhoj, Sukhna and Pichola; Chilka is not among them.

new.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is legally a:
new.x: NMCG, set up in 2011 as NGRBA's implementing arm, is a registered society.

new.s: In the Ganga governance structure, the Empowered Task Force is chaired by the:
new.x: The National Ganga Council is chaired by the PM; the Empowered Task Force by the Jal Shakti Minister.

new.s: Namami Gange-II, approved in 2022, has an outlay of:
new.x: Phase II (2021-2026) has ₹22,500 crore; Phase I had ₹20,000 crore.

new.s: The Global River Cities Alliance is led by:
new.x: GRCA, launched at COP28 Dubai, is led by NMCG under Jal Shakti.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Global River Cities Alliance:
1. It was launched at COP28 in Dubai.
2. It is led by the National Mission for Clean Ganga.
3. Its members are only Indian river cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: GRCA was launched at COP28 Dubai and is led by NMCG; its members include river cities worldwide, partner countries and funding agencies.

new.s: Ganga Praharis are:
o: Trained local volunteers for river biodiversity
new.x: Ganga Praharis are trained volunteers; JALAJ are livelihood centres, Ganga Utsav the festival and Arth Ganga the economy.

new.s: Which State has the most polluted river stretches identified by the CPCB?
new.x: Maharashtra has the most polluted stretches, 54.

new.s: In NITI Aayog's CWMI 2018, India ranked ____ of 122 countries in the water quality index cited.
new.x: CWMI 2018 placed India 120th of 122 countries.

new.s: The latest CPCB report (2026) lists how many polluted river stretches?
new.x: The count fell from 351 (2018) to 311 (2022) and 296 (2026) on 271 rivers.

new.s: Through which channel does Rajamahendravaram discharge sewage into the Godavari?
new.x: The municipal corporation discharges 29.6 MLD sewage through the Nalla Channel.

new.s: Which industrial unit is a main polluter of the Godavari near Rajamahendravaram?
new.x: Andhra Paper Ltd (31,934 KLD) and the Nalla Channel are the main polluters there.

new.s: The APPCB flagged high BOD and coliform in the Godavari ahead of the Pushkarams of:
new.x: The APPCB flag (June 2026) came ahead of the 2027 Godavari Pushkarams.
